findings.decompiled: mem[1031 len 65] = r, s, Bytes(1, v) / mem[899] = 196 / mem[931 len 4] = 371636862 / idx = 0 / while idx < 196: mem[idx + 1127] = mem[idx + 931]; idx = idx + 32 / static call owner with: args mem[1127 len 196]
findings.issue: The ERC-1271 fallback call copies its calldata through a while (constant bound 196 in the first permit, the signature length in the second) and writes the selector as a 4-byte integer piece, so the call prints as 'static call owner with: args mem[1127 len 196]' instead of isValidSignature(digest, signature).
findings.rule: A word-copy loop with a constant (or known) bound is a copy line; constant byte-range writes merge into the word they belong to; the buffer then decodes as a call with its selector and arguments.

notes: ERC-20 + permit token; all 25 functions compared line by line (transfer/transferFrom/approve with the Usds/* messages, mint/burn with wards and allowance, the two permit variants including the 65-byte ecrecover path and the ERC-1271 fallback, the domain separator built from constants, chainid and this.address). No source loops; the three whiles are implicit copies (P7). No semantic problem found.
summary: Small, complete and faithful; only the ERC-1271 isValidSignature calls lose their name and arguments because their calldata is copied through a loop.
